recentItems.title: Far-right election victory in Germany| US envoys visit Ukraine | India building collapse
recentItems.description:
Germany's AfD has claimed victory in a regional election, marking the first win by a far-right party in the country since World War Two. 

The Alternative for Germany party secured about 44 percent of the vote in the east German state of Saxony-Anhalt. 

The result falls short of an outright majority, but the party believes it has won a mandate to govern.

recentItems.title: FIFA boss Gianni Infantino confirms 2027 run
recentItems.description:
After facing backlash over his plan to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors, there have been questions about whether FIFA president Gianni Infantino has the support he needs to stay in the top job.

Despite the controversy, FIFA has confirmed that “nothing has changed” and the football CEO will stand for re-election next year.

recentItems.title: Tensions grow over tourism in Palau
recentItems.description:
Palau's president has accused China of 'weaponising tourism', after geopolitical tensions between the countries have reignited.

The Chinese government warned its residents not to travel to the Pacific Island, a tactic historically believed to punish Palau for their recognition of Taiwan.

Now, Australia is trying to support tourism in the region.

SBS Political correspondent Rayane Tamer reports from Palau's Rock Islands Southern Lagoon.

recentItems.title: US envoys attend peace talks in Moscow and Kyiv
recentItems.description:
Despite the latest push from the United States to speak to the leaders of Russia and Ukraine in their respective capitals, a breakthrough in peace negotiations appears no closer.

The US delegation said that "substantive plans will be announced in the coming weeks" during its stay in Moscow.

US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy both gave upbeat assessments of the talks, but neither announced any breakthroughs on ending the war with Russia.

Sunday's trip to Kyiv was their first visit to the Ukrainian capital, which has been hit by deadly Russian strikes for more than four years.

Read more: https://bit.ly/4gMIsUw

recentItems.title: Flag burning would be outlawed by Coalition
recentItems.description:
The Federal Coalition has unveiled new legislative proposals outlawing the burning of the Australian flag and defacing war memorials in a raft of new policy to be discussed in Canberra this week.

In addition, the Labor government is planning this week to unveil new policy to combat misogynistic content online along with an opt out policy for algorithms on social media platforms.

recentItems.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: Renewed sense of hope after people rescued from flooded tunnels
recentItems.description:
Three people have been found alive from different flooded tunnels in Nepal over the weekend following extensive search and rescue operations, 10 days after devastating floods swept through the country.

At least 1,344 people have been killed in Nepal in the floods that swept away houses, streets and schools in towns and villages near the border with China's Tibet, the disaster management authority said on Saturday.

An Australian team has arrived in Nepal to help search for those still missing — with 36 Australians among the more than 5,000 people unaccounted for as search crews continue to work through flood-hit communities.

As of Saturday, China said the death toll in Tibet was 31, with 531 others listed as missing, according to state media Xinhua.

recentItems.title: Tony Mundine's family pays tribute to the late champion
recentItems.description:
The family of boxing great Tony Mundine OAM has spoken publicly for the first time since his death at a service held in inner-city Sydney, describing the proud Bundjalung man as a mentor "who offered a home away from home for many".

The Bundjalung boxing legend, who died on Sunday aged 75, was a champion who became the first Australian to fight in four different weight divisions.

He was remembered not only for his achievements in sport but also for his dedication to family and community.
